signature: SUBROUTINE ZGGQRF( N, M, P, A, LDA, TAUA, B, LDB, TAUB, WORK,

params.name: N
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: M
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.

params.name: P
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrix B. $P \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-M matrix A. On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal of the array contain the min(N,M)-by-M upper trapezoidal matrix R (R is upper triangular if $N \ge M$); the elements below the diagonal, with the array `TAUA`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of min(N,M) elementary reflectors (see Further Details).

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: TAUA
params.reference: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the unitary matrix Q (see Further Details).

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-P matrix B. On exit, if $N \le P$, the upper triangle of the subarray `B(1:N,P-N+1:P)` contains the N-by-N upper triangular matrix T; if $N > P$, the elements on and above the (N-P)-th subdiagonal contain the N-by-P upper trapezoidal matrix T; the remaining elements, with the array `TAUB`, represent the unitary matrix Z as a product of elementary reflectors (see Further Details).

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: TAUB
params.reference: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the unitary matrix Z (see Further Details).

params.name: WORK

minLength.js: max( max( max( 1, N ), M ), P )

params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,N,M,P)$. For optimum performance $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (N,M,P) \, \max (\mathrm{NB1},\mathrm{NB2},\mathrm{NB3})$, where NB1 is the optimal blocksize for the QR factorization of an N-by-M matrix, NB2 is the optimal blocksize for the RQ factorization of an N-by-P matrix, and NB3 is the optimal blocksize for a call of ZUNMQR.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
